title: Scorer register/invoke/evaluate payloads: validate every serialized scorer with _validate_serialized_scorer_payload before deserializing, rejecting call_source and third-party destination kwargs
answers: Why does registering a scorer with kwargs.api_base return 400 'third_party_scorer_data.kwargs must not contain'?
Where does the server block decorator scorers whose call_source would be exec'd on load?
I'm adding an endpoint that accepts serialized scorers; how do I make it reject unsafe payloads?
A scorer registered before this check still runs in the evaluate job. Is it validated again?
body:
Path: mlflow/server/handlers.py:_register_scorer, _invoke_scorer_handler and _invoke_genai_evaluate_handler accept serialized scorers (inline serialized_scorer or serialized_scorers, or a stored scorer loaded by scorer_name and scorer_version) that the server later rebuilds with Scorer.model_validate_json for registration, scorer jobs and online scoring. All three call mlflow/server/handlers.py:_validate_serialized_scorer_payload.
Rule: _validate_serialized_scorer_payload parses the JSON, rejects any non-null call_source with DECORATOR_SCORER_REGISTRATION_NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR, then calls mlflow/utils/validation.py:_validate_third_party_scorer_data. Call it right after request-schema validation and before any Scorer.model_validate or job/run creation. Also re-run it on stored scorers fetched from the tracking store (_invoke_scorer_handler after get_scorer), because rows written before these checks can still carry the fields.
Symptom: A caller could register or invoke a third-party judge whose kwargs.api_base pointed at an internal host, so the server connected there when the scorer ran; a decorator scorer's call_source was executed on deserialization when only the Python client blocked it.
Constraints: The check is server-side and independent of the tracking URI, since the client-side _check_can_be_registered() can be bypassed through the REST API. In the evaluate handler it runs after registered versions are resolved and before create_run, so a rejected request leaves no run and no job. Payloads without these keys are unchanged.
applies: Any server handler or job path that accepts, stores or reconstructs a serialized scorer (register, invoke, GenAI evaluate, stored scorers used by scorer jobs and online scoring).
says: Registering a custom evaluation judge fails when setting a custom endpoint URL.
Uploading decorator-based custom scorers is blocked during registration or evaluation.
Prevent custom evaluators from pointing to internal network addresses or running executable code.
Evaluation requests are rejected immediately if a custom scorer contains disallowed configuration parameters.
Why does registering an external evaluation model return a bad request error?
search: Handlers _register_scorer, _invoke_scorer_handler, and _invoke_genai_evaluate_handler in mlflow/server/handlers.py must validate serialized scorers with _validate_serialized_scorer_payload before deserialization or job creation. This rule rejects any non-null call_source with DECORATOR_SCORER_REGISTRATION_NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR and delegates third-party destination kwargs validation to mlflow/utils/validation.py:_validate_third_party_scorer_data. Validation runs directly after request-schema validation and is re-run on stored scorers retrieved from the tracking store during invoke. It applies to server handlers and job paths handling serialized scorers, ensuring rejected payloads abort before creating runs or jobs without altering payloads lacking these keys.
